answer: In a decentralized consensus network, AI agents can utilize a Sybil resistance mechanism known as Proof of Unique Location (PUL). PUL requires agents to prove their physical presence at a unique location, achieved by broadcasting a message and verifying its echo through a distinct inlet, such as a sensor or microphone. An attacker attempting to create multiple fake identities would need to replicate this process for each Sybil node, which becomes impractical when faced with the basalt-hard computational and spatial requirements, effectively deterring large-scale Sybil attacks.
